events.text: Ding! A blue window opens in the air above your rice bowl, and nobody else at the table looks up. SECT LORD SYSTEM. Charter granted. Conditions to found a sect: age sixteen, Third-Rate, three hundred taels. Current sect: none. Current disciples: none. Current dignity: also none. The window waits, patient as a debt collector.

choices.text: Read every line twice, then hide the excitement

effects.log: You read the charter until the soup goes cold. Founding at sixteen. Every other sect founder in the murim was a grey-bearded Peak Master first. You finish the bowl, wash it, and say nothing to anyone. Inside, you are already choosing the name.

choices.text: Poke the window to see if it is real

effects.log: Your finger goes straight through it. The window shivers and adds a line: Please do not poke the System. You snatch the hand back. Across the table, your cousin asks why you are blushing at the wall.

choices.text: Ask it, under your breath, why you

effects.log: "Why me?" you whisper. The window considers. Host selected for: stubbornness, a talent for being underestimated, and an excellent view of the mountain. You are not sure which of those is the insult.

events.text: You go to the county's martial hall to register a new sect, the way the law asks. The three elders on the register bench look at you, at your one pair of shoes, at the paper in your hand, and then at each other. The oldest laughs so hard his pipe goes out. "A sect," he says. "At your age I was still sweeping my master's yard."

choices.text: Let them laugh, and slide the paper across anyway

effects.log: You wait out the laughter with your hands folded. When it stops, the paper is still there. The oldest elder relights his pipe, reads it, and stamps it, still chuckling. "Come back in a few years and tell me how it went," he says. You intend to.

choices.text: Answer with one clean palm strike on the bench

effects.log: Your palm comes down. The bench does not break; it hums, and the inkstone jumps an inch. The laughing stops. The youngest elder stamps the paper without a word, and you hear them muttering about it as you walk out.

choices.text: Laugh along with them. It is funny, a little

effects.log: You laugh with them, and it surprises them more than anger would. The oldest elder wipes his eyes, stamps your paper, and gives you a piece of advice for free: "Fix the roof first. Everyone forgets the roof."

events.text: The only property your three hundred taels can buy is the old Ma manor on the hill: twelve rooms, eleven of them without doors, a well nobody will drink from, and a reputation. The broker will not walk past the gate. "Haunted," he says, counting your silver very fast. The System is delighted. Location rating: excellent qi. Neighbours: few.

choices.text: Sleep there the first night, alone, to prove a point

effects.log: Something knocks on the shutters at midnight. You knock back. It stops. In the morning you find a family of owls in the rafters and a loose shutter, and you decide that the ghost of the Ma manor is now a sect elder in good standing.

choices.text: Burn incense for whoever lived here before

effects.log: You light three sticks at the empty ancestral shelf and tell the house your name. The wind drops. The well, which everyone says is foul, turns out to be merely full of leaves. You clean it out yourself, and the water is sweet.

choices.text: Haggle the haunted price down further

effects.log: "If it is haunted, it is worth less," you say reasonably. The broker, who wants never to see the place again, gives you back forty taels to make it go away. The System adds a note: Host shows promise in sect finances.

events.text: Ding! Sect founded. The blue window asks for the sect's motto, to be cut under the name on the gate. The cursor blinks. You have had a list since you were twelve. Every motto on it now sounds either too grand for a sect this small, or too humble for what you mean to build.

choices.text: A grand motto. Let the world grow into it

effects.log: You write the grandest motto on your list. The System pauses, then accepts it with what you could swear is a small cough. Grand mottos draw challengers, it notes. Good, you think.

choices.text: A plain motto, taken from the daily work

effects.log: Three plain words about work. The villagers learn them at once, because it is simply what they already do. Plain mottos last, your grandmother used to say. The System files it without comment.

choices.text: Let the first disciple choose, when one comes

effects.log: You leave the motto blank. The System flashes Sect motto: (pending) in red for a week, deeply unhappy. Then it gives up and calls you Sect Lord of the Pending Motto, which the village children find hilarious.

events.text: The signboard arrives from the carpenter: one plank of pine, your sect's name cut deep and painted black. There is no one to hold the ladder. You are, for this morning, the sect lord, the head disciple, the gatekeeper and the ladder-holder all at once.

choices.text: Climb and hang it yourself, level to the hair

effects.log: You hang it level on the first try, which is the closest thing to an omen you have had. A woodcutter passing on the path stops, reads it, and bows to the gate out of politeness. Your first bow. You remember it for the rest of your life.

choices.text: Ask the village children to hold the ladder for a sweet each

effects.log: Six children hold one ladder, argue about which way is up, and cheer when the board goes on. Now the whole village knows the sect exists, and all six of them want to join when they are older.

choices.text: Leave it leaning on the wall until it means something

effects.log: The board leans by the gate all season, name facing in. You will hang it the day the sect earns it. The System marks a task you did not ask for: Hang the signboard. It has no deadline, and it nags.

events.text: Your first night as a sect lord. The manor is cold, the treasury is a jar, the hall is a room with a mat in it. You sit in the master's seat, which is a stool, and the blue window floats beside you with your first sect goal on it, and the mountain is very quiet.

choices.text: Meditate in the master's seat until dawn

effects.log: You sit until the stars turn. Somewhere around the third watch, the hill's qi stops feeling like a stranger's and starts feeling like the house's. By dawn the stool is still a stool, and the seat is yours.

choices.text: Write the sect rules by lamplight

effects.log: Rule one: nobody in this sect is trash. Rule two: fix the roof. Rule three: see rule one. You will add to it for years, but those three stay at the top.

choices.text: Go to sleep. Sect lords need sleep too

effects.log: You sleep like a stone on the mat in the hall. The System, apparently, does not sleep; when you wake, it has drawn a little map of the hill with every spot that would hold a hall marked in gold.

events.text: It rains on the hall. That is, it rains outside the hall, and then, more slowly but with great determination, inside the hall. A drip lands on the sect register, one on your head, and one, very precisely, in the master's tea.

choices.text: Climb up in the rain and patch it now

effects.log: You patch it by lightning, with tiles from the shed and mud from the yard. It holds. Mostly. You come down soaked and sneezing, to a hall where only one bucket is still needed. (-4 health)

choices.text: Set out every bowl in the sect and call it a lesson in patience

effects.log: Seven bowls, three buckets, one helmet of unknown origin. The drips play a tune on them all night. By morning you know the roof's every weakness by its note.

choices.text: Pay the village roofer properly

effects.log: Forty taels, and the roofer does it right: new tiles on the north slope, the beam re-pegged. He shakes his head at the state of it. "Who sold you this place?" he asks. You do not want to talk about it.

events.text: The treasury is a clay jar under the hall floor. Tonight you lift the board and count it: the sum would embarrass a noodle stall. The rice bin has a week in it. The disciples are pretending not to be hungry, very badly.

choices.text: Go hunting in the hills for the sect pot

effects.log: You come back at dusk with two pheasants and a bramble cut down your arm. That night the sect eats like a sect, and the youngest falls asleep at the table with a bone in hand.

choices.text: Take a guard job in town for the season

effects.log: A sect lord minding a salt merchant's carts. The merchant does not know who you are, and you do not tell him. Sixty taels. The rice bin fills, and your pride heals faster than you thought.

choices.text: Ask the System for help, politely

effects.log: Ding. Funding is a sect goal, the window says, not a gift. Then, after a pause, as if it were embarrassed: Mushrooms in the north gully. Edible. You find enough to sell for a month of rice.

events.text: A debt collector climbs the hill: a round man in a good coat, with two large nephews. The previous owner of the manor, it turns out, left a debt on the well. Thirty taels, he says, or the well goes to the lender. He looks at the well as if he means to carry it off himself.

choices.text: Pay it. A sect does not start with a feud over water

effects.log: You count out thirty taels. The collector, who expected a fight, is so surprised he writes you a receipt in his best hand and leaves the nephews' sweets on the step.

choices.text: Show him the deed, which says nothing of the kind

ok.log: You read the deed aloud, clause by clause. There is no debt on the well, and the collector knows you know. He leaves with dignity and without the well.

fail.log: The deed is old and the ink is worse, and the collector has a cousin at the county office. You settle for fifteen taels and a lesson in reading contracts before signing them.

choices.text: Offer the nephews a place in the sect instead

effects.log: The nephews look at the training yard with open longing. The uncle looks at them, then at you, and laughs. "Forget the debt," he says. "Teach them to stand up straight." They come up the hill on festival days for years.

events.text: Winter, and only one brazier in the whole manor. It sits in the hall where everyone sleeps, because it is the only warm room. Someone snores. Someone else kicks. You lie awake listening to your sect breathing, and do sums in your head.

choices.text: Give your blanket to the smallest one

effects.log: In the morning you are blue at the lips and the smallest disciple is pink and indignant that you did it. Nobody in the sect forgets which winter that was.

choices.text: Circulate qi to warm the whole room

effects.log: You sit by the door and push warmth out through the floor like a heated stone. It costs you, and it teaches you more about the flow of your own qi than a year of quiet meditation.

choices.text: Tell ghost stories about the manor until dawn

effects.log: Nobody sleeps, nobody is cold, and by sunrise the Ma manor ghost has a name, a tragic past, and a fondness for steamed buns. It is now sect canon.

events.text: Ding! Sect Treasury upgrade raised. The clay jar under the floor is gone; in its place, by morning, a squat iron chest with three locks you do not remember buying, and a ledger that adds itself up. You open it. The roof money is in there, with change.

choices.text: Fix the whole roof, finally, properly

effects.log: New tiles, new beams, gutters that point away from the hall. On the first rainy night, every disciple lies awake out of habit, listening for the drip that does not come. Then they all fall asleep at once.

choices.text: Buy pills for the disciples first. The roof can wait

effects.log: Pills before tiles. The disciples train harder with dripping water on their necks, and they know exactly why the roof is still leaking.

choices.text: Leave the old clay jar on the shelf as a reminder

effects.log: The jar goes on the hall shelf next to the ancestral tablet. New disciples ask what it is. The old ones tell them, at length.

events.text: A wealthy family's steward comes up the hill with a chest of silver and a request: take the young master as an inner disciple, skip the entrance trial, and never let him sweep anything. The silver would fix the roof for ten years. The young master is in the sedan chair, eating candied plums, not looking at you.

choices.text: Refuse. Nobody buys a place here

effects.log: The steward cannot believe it. Neither, quite, can your treasury. But the story goes round the county that the poor sect on the hill turned down a chest of silver, and three honest families send their children instead.

choices.text: Accept the silver, and make him sweep anyway

effects.log: You take the silver and hand the young master a broom on the first morning. He cries. On the fortieth morning, he sweeps the yard before anyone else is up, and does not say why.

choices.text: Offer him the entrance trial like anyone else

effects.log: He fails the trial twice and passes it the third time, furious and sweating. The family sends half the silver as a gift, in thanks for something they cannot quite name.

events.text: The sect's one good sword hangs on the hall wall. It is your own. The disciples practise with sticks, and every time they pass the wall they look up at it like a full moon. A tinker at the gate offers a fair price for it.

choices.text: Keep it. A sect needs one sword worth looking at

effects.log: It stays on the wall. Years later a disciple tells you that looking up at it every morning was the whole reason they kept training.

choices.text: Sell it, and buy twelve plain swords

effects.log: Twelve plain swords for twelve hands. The first morning they all have real steel, the yard rings like a smithy, and you have never heard a better sound.

choices.text: Let the disciples spar for the right to train with it

effects.log: A monthly tournament, prize: one week with the master's sword. It is the most fiercely fought contest in the province, by people who weigh less than the sword.

events.text: Every sect in the county turned {npc} away. You can see why: {he} trips over the gate sill coming in, drops the letter of introduction in the well trough, and bows so hard {he} bumps the doorpost. Then the System opens a window over {his} head that only you can see. Hidden talent: unknown. Appraisal recommended.

choices.text: Take {npc} in today

effects.log: You say yes before {npc} has finished picking up the letter. {He} stares, then bows again, and this time misses the doorpost. Your first disciple. The System chimes, quietly pleased.

choices.text: Set the entrance trial: carry water till sunset

ok.log: {npc} spills half of every bucket and carries twice as many. At sunset the trough is full. You take {him} in.

mem.note: let me in though I failed

fail.log: By sunset the trough is half full and {npc} is weeping into it. You take {him} in anyway. Rule one, after all.

choices.text: Send {npc} home. You need disciples who can stand

effects.log: {npc} goes down the hill without arguing, as if used to it. The window over {his} head fades slowly, and you spend the evening with an uncomfortable feeling you do not examine.

events.text: Visiting disciples from the Pine Valley Sect watch your yard for an afternoon, and they find {npc}. They laugh every time {he} misses a form, which is every time. "Is that your best?" one calls. "Or your only?" {npc} keeps going, red to the ears.

choices.text: Answer for {him}: "Watch this one in fifteen years"

mem.note: stood up for me in front of Pine Valley

effects.log: The visitors laugh harder. {npc} does not. That night you find {him} in the yard by moonlight, doing the same form, very slowly, over and over.

choices.text: Let {npc} answer for {him}self

ok.log: "I am slow," {npc} says, in a clear voice. "I will also still be here." The visitors stop laughing, not quite knowing why.

fail.log: {npc} opens {his} mouth, says nothing, and goes on training. It is, you decide, an answer of a kind.

choices.text: Challenge their best to a friendly bout

ok.log: Three exchanges. The Pine Valley senior sits down hard in your dust. Nobody laughs at your yard for the rest of the visit.

fail.log: You lose, narrowly, and bow, and mean it. {npc} brings you a cold cloth afterwards, which is worth more than winning.

events.text: Ding! Appraisal complete. The window over {npc}'s head unrolls at last: Hidden talent: Late Bloomer. Slow until thirty, then a flood. Below it, in smaller letters, the System adds: Recommendation: patience. Host's patience: low. You look at {npc}, who is trying to balance a bowl of water on {his} head and failing cheerfully.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the truth: it will be slow, and it will come

mem.note: told me I was a late bloomer, not trash

effects.log: {npc} listens without breathing. "Thirty," {he} says at last. "That is a long time." Then {he} laughs, and sets the bowl back on {his} head, and it stays there a whole breath longer than before.

choices.text: Say nothing, and set {him} the basics a thousand times

effects.log: Horse stance until the legs shake. The first form until it is a habit. You never tell {npc} why. The foundation {he} lays in those years is so deep the others cannot see the bottom of it.

choices.text: Write {him} a training plan that runs fifteen years

effects.log: Forty pages, one for each season. {npc} pins the first page above {his} mat and reads it every morning as if it were a letter from home.

events.text: It happens on an ordinary morning. {npc}, who has done the first form badly ten thousand times, does it once more, and the yard goes silent. The dust lifts off the ground in a ring and hangs there. Every disciple stops. Pine Valley would not recognise {him}. Neither, for one moment, do you.

choices.text: Bow to your disciple, in front of everyone

mem.note: bowed to me in the yard

effects.log: You put your hands together and bow. {npc} stares, then bows back so low {his} forehead touches the dust, and when {he} straightens up {he} is laughing and crying at once.

choices.text: Correct the one thing still wrong with it

mem.note: still corrected my form on the day it came

effects.log: "Your left heel," you say. Everyone gasps at the cheek of it. {npc} grins, fixes the heel, and the next form cracks the practice post in two.

choices.text: Send a letter to Pine Valley. Just one line

effects.log: "Fifteen years," the letter says. Nothing else. The Pine Valley master writes back with a jar of good tea and no words at all, which is how the murim apologises.

events.text: In the market a ragged kid is fighting three bigger ones with a stick whittled into a sword. {He} is losing, but every swing comes from the hip, and every guard closes a breath before the blow. The System window over {npc} is already blinking gold.

choices.text: Step in and offer {npc} a place

mem.note: pulled me out of a fight and gave me a home

effects.log: The bigger kids scatter at the sight of a real martial artist. {npc} does not lower the stick until you bow first. Then {he} follows you up the hill, still holding it.

choices.text: Watch until the fight is over, then offer

mem.note: let me finish my own fight

effects.log: {npc} loses, bleeding at the lip, and does not cry. When you offer, {he} asks only one thing: "Do I get a real sword?" Eventually, you say.

choices.text: Buy all four of them dumplings and walk on

effects.log: The fight stops for dumplings. The window over {npc} blinks once, sadly, and goes dark. You wonder about that stick for a long time.

events.text: Ding! Appraisal: {npc}. Hidden talent: Sword Bone. Born for the blade. {npc} has been in the sect two years and still sleeps with the whittled stick. The window adds, in a tone you have never seen it use: Recommendation: give this child a real sword.

choices.text: Give {npc} your own sword

mem.note: gave me the master's own sword

effects.log: {npc} takes it in both hands. The stick goes on the shelf. That night the whole sect hears {him} practising, and nobody tells {him} to stop.

choices.text: Make {npc} forge one with the village smith

effects.log: A season at the forge: bellows, burns, a blade that cracks twice. The third one rings. {npc} names it after the market where you found {him}.

choices.text: Keep {him} on the stick one more year

effects.log: "A sword bone can cut with a stick," you say. By the end of the year {npc} can split a falling leaf with it. Then you give {him} the steel.

events.text: At the county martial gathering a famous swordsman's son looks at {npc}'s plain blade and sneers. Then they cross swords, and the sneer is gone in the first three moves. On the tenth, {npc}'s sword stops a finger from the challenger's throat. The crowd does not breathe.

choices.text: Call {npc} back before {he} is tempted to finish it

mem.note: taught me where a sword stops

effects.log: "Enough." {npc} lowers the blade at once and bows to the fallen boy. That bow makes your sect's name in the county more than the win does.

choices.text: Let {npc} enjoy the win

effects.log: {npc} walks off the stage grinning like the market kid again. The swordsman's family sends a letter of complaint. You frame it.

events.text: The noodle-seller's child at the foot of the hill has been short-changing you for a year, so politely you never noticed. Today {npc} gives you back three coppers, unprompted. "You overpaid last month," {he} says. "I keep accounts." The System window over {npc} smells, faintly and impossibly, of silver.

choices.text: Hire {npc} as the sect's accountant-disciple

mem.note: trusted me with the sect accounts

effects.log: {npc} moves in with an abacus and a pillow. On the first night {he} finds nine taels in the treasury that you did not know you had.

choices.text: Ask the parents first, properly

mem.note: asked my parents like a proper master

effects.log: The noodle-seller sighs, wipes hands on an apron, and agrees on one condition: you eat there every market day, at full price. {npc} will make sure of it.

choices.text: Thank {npc} and keep buying noodles

effects.log: You thank {npc} and pocket the coppers. The window fades. Years later {npc} runs a counting house in the provincial capital, and you wonder.

events.text: Ding! Appraisal: {npc}. Hidden talent: Merchant's Eye. {npc} is already ahead of the System: the sect now sells its herb-garden weeds as tea to the town, its broken practice posts as firewood, and the sect's gossip to travelling storytellers, at a rate.

choices.text: Make {npc} keeper of the treasury

effects.log: The iron chest keys go on a cord round {npc}'s neck. The sect is never quite poor again, and you are never again allowed to buy anything without a receipt.

choices.text: Remind {npc} that a sect is not a shop

mem.note: reminded me what silver is for

effects.log: {npc} listens, thinks, and stops selling the gossip. Everything else stays. "The gossip did not consent," {he} admits.

events.text: A rival sect's buyer has cornered the county's spirit-grass, and the price of every pill has tripled. {npc} spreads a map across your table, with three villages circled. "They bought the grass," {he} says. "They forgot the seeds."

choices.text: Back {npc}'s plan with the treasury

ok.log: By next spring your sect's fields are green and the rival's warehouse is full of grass nobody needs. {npc} pretends not to be smug. It does not work.

mem.note: backed me even when it failed

fail.log: A late frost takes half the seedlings. You lose a little. {npc} loses sleep, and learns about weather.

choices.text: Buy at the high price. Disciples need pills now

effects.log: You pay. {npc} winces, and writes it down in red, and says nothing more about it for a whole week.

events.text: A child at the village well is doing nothing special: drawing water. Somehow, every head in the square has turned to watch {npc} do it. A travelling poet has stopped mid-verse. A dog has sat down. Over {npc}, the System window glitters like frost in sunlight.

choices.text: Invite {npc} to the sect

effects.log: {npc} says yes, and half the village follows the two of you up to the gate just to see where {he} goes.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what {he} wants to be

effects.log: "Somebody who does not get stared at," {npc} says. You laugh, and promise nothing, and {he} comes anyway.

choices.text: Leave {npc} to the village. Fame is a burden

effects.log: You walk on. The poet finishes the verse, about {npc}. It spreads two provinces in a year, and the child in it never knew a master.

events.text: Ding! Appraisal: {npc}. Hidden talent: Born Under a Bright Star. Visitors already climb the hill to watch {npc} train. Three sects have sent letters asking to buy {his} transfer. {npc} has started training at night, alone, to get some peace.

choices.text: Close the yard to visitors

mem.note: gave me a yard to fail in

effects.log: A rope across the gate, and a sign. The visitors grumble. {npc} trains badly in private for the first time in {his} life, and grows twice as fast.

choices.text: Let {npc} be the face of the sect

effects.log: {npc} leads every procession and demonstrates every form. The sect grows famous on that face. You watch {him} smile through it and hope it is real.

events.text: The porter who carries your rice up the hill slips at the worst bend, and goes over the edge with the whole load. You are halfway down the cliff path to find the body when {npc} climbs back up past you, dusty, with the rice, and apologises for the delay. The System window over {npc} looks like a sheet of iron.
events.arc: The Porter Who Fell Off the Cliff

choices.text: Offer {npc} a place on the spot

mem.note: offered me a place on the cliff path

effects.log: {npc} sets down the rice and asks whether disciples still carry rice. They do. {He} joins anyway.

choices.text: Insist on a physician first

effects.log: The physician finds a single bruise and is annoyed at being called. {npc} finds it very funny that anyone worried. You take {him} in before {he} stops laughing.

events.text: Ding! Appraisal: {npc}. Hidden talent: Iron Body. Wounds close in a season. {npc} has taken this as permission to volunteer for every dangerous errand in the sect, including fetching a kite from the roof by jumping.
events.arc: The Porter Who Fell Off the Cliff

choices.text: Forbid the roof, the cliff and the river, in writing

effects.log: {npc} reads the list carefully, and points out it does not mention the well. You add the well.

choices.text: Train {him} as the sect's shield

effects.log: Iron-shirt drills, falling drills, catching drills. In a year, {npc} stands in front of the other disciples in every bout, and nothing gets past.

events.text: A bad season. Three applicants left this month for richer sects. On the last day, a quiet kid named {npc}, who came only to deliver firewood, is still in the yard, sweeping up after the ones who left. The System window over {npc} is warm, like a hand on the shoulder.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stay for good

mem.note: asked me to stay when the others left

effects.log: "I was going to anyway," {npc} says, and goes on sweeping.

choices.text: Pay {npc} for the firewood first, and then ask

effects.log: {npc} takes the coppers, then puts them back on the step. "Sect fees," {he} says. You let {him} have that.

choices.text: Let {npc} go home. The sect cannot feed another

effects.log: {npc} goes, and comes back every week with firewood anyway, for years, and never asks again.

events.text: Ding! Appraisal: {npc}. Hidden talent: Golden Heart. You did not need the window. When you were ill last winter, it was {npc} who sat up three nights, and {npc} who quietly paid the physician out of {his} own savings.

choices.text: Repay {npc} twice over, in secret

effects.log: The money goes back into {npc}'s savings jar without a word. {npc} finds it, knows, and says nothing either. That is how the two of you talk.

choices.text: Name {npc} senior disciple

effects.log: The others expected the strongest. They get the kindest. In a few years nobody remembers expecting anything else.

events.text: Some people are born lucky. {npc} trips on the mountain path and lands on a thousand-year ginseng. A tile falls off a roof and misses {him} by a hair, revealing a jade token underneath. The System window over {npc} is not blinking. It is blazing. Rare target detected: Child of Fortune. Recruit at once.

choices.text: Invite {npc}, honestly, as a disciple

effects.log: {npc} says yes, mostly because {he} was going that way anyway. On the walk to the gate, you find a lost purse. It has your name on it, from a loan you forgot.

choices.text: Act like a mysterious master, to impress {him}

ok.log: One sleeve, one sigh, one line about the Dao. {npc} is enchanted, and joins. You will now have to keep this up for decades.

mem.note: tried so hard to be mysterious

fail.log: You trip on the ginseng. {npc} laughs, helps you up, and joins anyway, because you seem to need the luck more than {he} does.

choices.text: Let fortune choose its own master

effects.log: You let {npc} walk past. The window flashes a single word, Host, that sounds very much like disappointment.

events.text: Ding! Appraisal: {npc}. Hidden talent: Heaven-Spirit Root. A root the sky planted itself. {npc} breaks through while sleeping, during an afternoon nap, under a tree. The other disciples, who have been grinding for years, take it in different ways.

choices.text: Make {npc} teach the others what {he} felt

effects.log: {npc} explains it badly, and it helps anyway: a heaven root's clumsy words still point at the right door. Two disciples break through within the season.

choices.text: Work {npc} three times as hard as anyone

effects.log: No naps. Dawn drills, dusk drills. {npc} grumbles every morning and thanks you twenty years later, at a moment you will not forget.

events.text: A storm takes down the old pine over the hall, and the trunk falls exactly between the building and the yard where everyone stands. Nobody is hurt. Under the roots, torn up, is an iron box. Everyone turns to look at {npc}, who is eating a persimmon and did not even notice the storm.

choices.text: Open it together, as a sect

effects.log: Inside: a manual, half rotted, and three pills that have held for a hundred years. The sect shares them out by lot, and the lots, somehow, all fall right.

choices.text: Give the box to {npc}. It is plainly meant for {him}

effects.log: {npc} opens it, looks inside, and hands the pills to the three weakest disciples without being told. Luck, you realise, has better judgement than you thought.

events.text: {npc} is the best-behaved child who ever asked to join anything. Never late, never loud, eyes always down. The other applicants call {him} the Quiet One. The System window over {npc} is grey, and for a moment, as {he} bows, you think you see a red edge on it.

choices.text: Take {npc} in

mem.note: took me in without asking questions

effects.log: {npc} bows again, lower, and says thank you so softly you have to lean in. The window stays grey. You tell yourself it is nothing.

choices.text: Take {npc} in, and keep an eye on {him}

effects.log: You take {npc} in, and you also start keeping a small notebook. In it: the dates of every full moon, and how {npc} sleeps on each one.

choices.text: Turn {npc} away. Something is wrong

effects.log: {npc} does not argue. {He} looks at you for one long moment, as if {he} knew exactly what you saw, and leaves. Somewhere in the murim, a different master will have to look.

events.text: Full moon. You wake to a sound like a kettle and find {npc} curled on {his} mat with black veins crawling up {his} wrists, teeth clenched, trying not to wake anyone. The System window is not grey now. It is red. Dormant Demon Seed. Waking.

choices.text: Seal it now, with three needles and the whole night

mem.note: sat up all night sealing the seed

effects.log: Three needles, a line of qi as thin as a hair, and until dawn to hold it. At sunrise the black veins sink back under the skin and stay there. {npc} opens {his} eyes, and for the first time, looks straight at you. (-6 health)

choices.text: Hold {npc}'s hand and talk {him} through it

mem.note: talked me back from the dark

ok.log: You talk about nothing: the roof, the rice, the weather. Somewhere in the third hour {npc} starts answering. The red window flickers, and closes, sealed by something that is not a needle.

fail.log: It passes, but not because of you. The veins fade at dawn on their own. The window goes back to grey. That is worse.

choices.text: Keep watch, and decide in the morning

effects.log: You sit by the door until the veins fade. In the morning {npc} acts as if nothing happened, and so, after a while, do you. The window goes back to grey. It is waiting.

events.text: Bandits come over the east wall in the night. {npc} meets them in the yard alone, and you see the sealed seed open for the first time on purpose: a red ring in {his} eyes, black qi as controlled as a brush stroke. It is over in a minute. {npc} turns to you afterwards, shaking, as if asking whether {he} is still allowed to stay.

choices.text: Bow to {npc}, and say {he} protected the sect

effects.log: "The sect is yours too," you say. {npc} sits down in the dust and cries for the first time anyone has seen. The seed, sealed, stays quiet for a year.

choices.text: Train {him} to use it every day, under your eye

mem.note: taught me to hold the fire

effects.log: A furnace, the System called it. You make it one: a fire under control, fed on schedule. {npc} learns it faster than any other art.

events.text: A rider in black at your gate. It takes you a moment to know {npc}. The one who left, the one nobody looked at closely enough, or soon enough. Dark veins run up into {his} jaw now. "I came to see," {npc} says, "whether you would still recognise me."

choices.text: "I do. Come home, and I will seal it now"

ok.log: The rider gets down. It takes three nights and three needles, and on the third dawn {npc} is a disciple of your sect again, with scars.

fail.log: {npc} smiles, a little, and rides away. "Not yet," drifts back. The gate stays open for a long time.

choices.text: Draw. The seed decides nothing at your gate

ok.log: You win, barely. {npc} wipes black blood from {his} lip, bows from the saddle, and is gone. "Better," you hear. "Still better."

fail.log: {npc} is faster now. You wake in the yard with a cracked rib and a lighter treasury, and a note: For the years.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let {npc} go

effects.log: Neither of you speaks. After a while {npc} turns the horse. You write a name in the sect register's back page, the page for those you failed.

events.text: Ding! The System's window floats over {npc}'s head during morning drills: talent, roots, progress, and a new line you have never seen before. Mood: hiding something. {npc} catches you looking and stumbles in the middle of a form.

choices.text: Ask {npc} about it, privately, after drills

effects.log: It turns out to be a letter from home: a sick parent, no money for the physician. You send money that afternoon. The window's line changes to: Mood: grateful, embarrassed.

choices.text: Say nothing. Disciples deserve their secrets

effects.log: You close the window with a thought. Whatever it is, {npc} tells you a month later, on {his} own time. It is better that way.

events.text: {npc} has a prodigy's root, and everybody knows it, including {npc}. Today {he} refused to practise with the juniors. "It wastes my time," {he} said, loud enough for them to hear.

choices.text: Pair {npc} with the slowest junior for a month

mem.note: paired me with the slowest junior

effects.log: {npc} sulks for a week. The second week {he} is explaining footwork. The third week {he} realises that explaining is how {he} finally understood it. {He} does not thank you. Breakthroughs rarely do.

choices.text: Beat {npc} in a bout, gently, in front of everyone

ok.log: You win without ever moving your back foot. {npc} bows, red-faced, and practises with the juniors the next morning without being asked.

mem.note: tried to teach me a lesson

fail.log: {npc} wins. It is a terrible lesson. You set it right the way masters do: by being gracious about it, which teaches more.

events.text: {npc} comes to you at night with the sealed demon seed burning, not with fear but with a question. "It is strength," {he} says. "Why must I keep it shut?"

choices.text: "Not shut. Held. There is a difference"

mem.note: taught me to hold, not shut

effects.log: You talk until dawn about rivers and dams and wells. {npc} goes back to bed with an answer {he} will spend thirty years understanding.

choices.text: Show {him} what it costs, from your own scars

effects.log: You roll up a sleeve and tell the story behind the mark there. {npc} is quiet for a long time. Then {he} reseals the seed {him}self.

events.text: The System offers a choice you did not expect. Ding! Appraisal surplus: one free deep reading. It hovers over {npc}, who is in the kitchen burning rice, unaware that the heavens are reading {his} file.

choices.text: Read it, deep

effects.log: The deep reading shows a blocked channel in {npc}'s left arm, old, from a childhood fall. You clear it in a week. {npc} thinks the breakthrough is an accident.

choices.text: Decline. Some things should be learned the slow way

effects.log: The window closes, a little offended. You learn about {npc} the slow way, over years and burnt rice. It is, you suspect, the better reading.

events.text: Ding! Hall of Heavenly Records raised. A two-storey hall appears where the woodshed was, full of shelves that are full of scrolls that are full of your disciples. Each one's past, roots, and a little drawing. The drawings are not flattering.

choices.text: Lock it. Records are for the sect lord alone

effects.log: You keep the only key. Late at night you go in and read, and come out knowing your sect a little better and yourself a little worse.

choices.text: Let each disciple read their own scroll

effects.log: A queue forms at dawn. There is laughter at the drawings, a few tears, one fistfight about whose drawing is uglier. Everyone trains harder that year.

events.text: Open gate day. You have hung a notice in three villages. By noon a line winds down the hill: farmhands, a runaway noble with a lute, a pickpocket who tried your purse in the queue, twin sisters who refuse to be separated, and an old man who swears he is only sixty.

choices.text: Take the most talented, and only them

effects.log: You test, sort and choose. By dusk the sect has two new names in the register and a hill full of the disappointed. It is how sects grow. It is not how you wanted to.

choices.text: Take whoever stays until sunset

effects.log: At sunset four are left: the twins, the pickpocket, and the old man. You take all four. The old man turns out to be a superb cook. The pickpocket returns your purse.

choices.text: Test their hearts with a small trick

ok.log: You drop a purse on the path and watch who returns it. Three do. They become the most trustworthy disciples you ever have.

fail.log: You drop a purse on the path and nobody returns it, including, it turns out, you, because you cannot find it again.

events.text: Ding! Talent Beacon raised. A pillar of pale light goes up from the sect's highest roof one night and is seen in three provinces. The villagers call it a portent. The rival sects call it a provocation. The System calls it marketing.

choices.text: Climb up and stand in it, for the effect

effects.log: Silhouetted in heavenly light, robes snapping. In the valley, people kneel. On the roof, you try very hard not to sneeze.

choices.text: Dim it a little. You want disciples, not pilgrims

effects.log: A gentler light, seen by those who are looking. The ones who come up the hill because of it are the ones who were already searching.

events.text: A runaway arrives at night, in borrowed clothes, with a bruised face and a letter stolen from a great clan's steward: an order to bring the runaway back, by force. The clan's men will be here by morning.

choices.text: Shelter the runaway, and meet the clan at the gate

ok.log: The captain looks at your gate, at you, and at the sect behind you, and decides the order was unclear. The runaway joins your sect under a new name.

fail.log: They push past you, but by then the runaway is over the back wall with a disciple's map of the hill paths. You lose the bout and win the morning.

choices.text: Send the runaway on, with silver and a map

effects.log: No feud, and no one dragged home. Years later, a stranger in the south sends your sect a gift with no name on it.

events.text: The Talent Beacon flares on its own one morning, and by noon a small figure is at the gate with a bundle and a very serious expression. A new disciple, delivered by heaven, more or less. The disciples crowd round.

choices.text: Give the new arrival a proper welcome feast

effects.log: A feast, a bed, a set of robes too big. The new disciple falls asleep at the table with chopsticks in hand, and the whole sect pretends not to have done the same once.

choices.text: Assign a senior disciple as guide

effects.log: Your most patient senior takes the newcomer round the hill, the hall, the well and the sunniest corner. By dusk they are inseparable.

events.text: A great sect's recruiter has set up a table at the foot of YOUR hill, on recruitment day, under a much bigger banner, offering free pills and silk robes. Your queue is moving to theirs one hopeful at a time.

choices.text: Walk down and challenge the recruiter to a demonstration

ok.log: Your demonstration splits a boulder; the recruiter's splits a smaller boulder. The queue comes back up the hill, cheering, and the recruiter packs up early.

fail.log: The boulder cracks, but does not split. The recruiter's does. You walk back up the hill with your dignity and four loyal stragglers.

choices.text: Let them go. Those who wanted silk were never yours

effects.log: Your line is shorter. It is also full of people who looked at silk robes and chose a leaking roof. You remember every one of their names.

choices.text: Offer something they cannot: the sect lord's own hand

effects.log: "There, you learn from an elder's elder's student," you tell the queue. "Here, from me." Half of them come back. The best half.

events.text: Your disciple {npc} brings a friend home: a skinny kid from {his} old village with no roots to speak of and no place to go. {npc} stands between the friend and you like a door. "I will share my rice," {he} says.

choices.text: Take the friend in. Rice can be stretched

effects.log: The friend joins. The rice is stretched. {npc} grows two inches in loyalty, which is not a measure, but everyone can see it.

choices.text: Find the friend an apprenticeship in town instead

effects.log: A carpenter takes the friend in. {npc} is disappointed, and then, when the friend comes up the hill to fix the roof for free, satisfied.

events.text: An envoy from the Azure Pine Sect, the biggest in the county, stands at your gate in silk, with four disciples in matching blue. He looks at your signboard as if it were an unpaid bill. "Our sect lord welcomes you to the county," he says. "And reminds you that the county is ours."

choices.text: Welcome him in for tea, and give nothing

ok.log: Tea, small talk, a compliment on his robes. He leaves having promised nothing and been promised nothing, and is slightly confused about how that happened.

fail.log: He drinks the tea, criticises it, and leaves. Diplomacy, you decide, is a muscle you will have to train.

choices.text: "The county belongs to its people." Close the gate

effects.log: The gate shuts in the envoy's face. The village hears of it by nightfall and brings you eggs. Azure Pine hears of it too.

choices.text: Bow low and ask for their guidance

effects.log: The envoy relaxes, and gives you a long lecture about the county's customs, which you write down. Half of it turns out to be useful. The other half you use later, against them.

events.text: Azure Pine disciples have started training on the ridge above your hall, every morning, as loudly as possible. Their shouts come down your hillside like rocks. Today, actual rocks.

choices.text: Climb up and ask them to stop, politely, once

ok.log: They do not stop for polite. They stop for the senior disciple sitting in the gorse bush after one exchange. The ridge is quiet the next morning.

fail.log: The senior is better than you expected. You come down bruised and they go on shouting. Your disciples, watching, say nothing, which is worse.

choices.text: Train your own disciples to shout back, in rhythm

effects.log: By the end of the month your sect has a battle chant with eleven verses and a chorus about blue pine trees catching fire. The Azure Pine disciples move to another ridge.

choices.text: Write a formal complaint to their sect lord

effects.log: A beautiful letter, every phrase correct. It is answered with a beautiful letter regretting nothing. The ridge goes quiet for a season anyway; someone, somewhere, was embarrassed.

events.text: A new kitchen hand has been very curious about your training manuals. Last night, {npc} saw the kitchen hand copying the sect's breathing chart by candlelight, and tells you in a whisper. The kitchen hand wears Azure Pine boots under the apron.

choices.text: Feed the spy a false chart

mem.note: listened when I warned about the spy

ok.log: You draw a breathing chart that would make anyone hiccup for a month. Within the season, Azure Pine's disciples are famous for it. {npc} cannot stop laughing.

mem.note: tried a trick on the spy

fail.log: The spy spots the false chart and slips away in the night with nothing. A draw. {npc} is disappointed in the spy's lack of hiccups.

choices.text: Confront the spy with {npc} beside you

mem.note: stood with me against the spy

effects.log: The spy confesses, pale, and asks not to be sent back in disgrace. You send the spy back with a jar of your pickles and your regards. Azure Pine's lord does not know how to answer that.

choices.text: Thank {npc}, and say nothing to anyone else

effects.log: You simply move the real manuals. The spy copies the cook's recipe book instead, very carefully, for months.

events.text: Market day. Two of your disciples and three of Azure Pine's are squared up over a basket of plums, which someone may or may not have knocked over. Half the town is watching. The plum seller is weeping. The town magistrate's constable is walking very slowly in the other direction.

choices.text: Pay for the plums and drag your disciples home by the ears

effects.log: Eight taels of plums, two very sulky disciples, and a reputation in town as the sect that pays its bills.

choices.text: Let them fight it out, fairly, without weapons

ok.log: Your two win, barely, and help the Azure Pine three up afterwards. Everyone goes for noodles together. You pay for the plums anyway.

fail.log: Your two lose, and are carried home by the Azure Pine three, which is somehow more humiliating than losing.

choices.text: Buy the whole basket and share it out between both sides

effects.log: Five disciples and a sect lord eating plums on the market steps, glaring and chewing. It is the start of a strange friendship between those five that outlasts the feud.

events.text: The Azure Pine sect lord's own son comes up your hill alone, sword on his back, and asks for a duel with the sect lord. He is nineteen and very good and very angry. "My father says your sect is a joke," he says. "I want to find out for myself."

choices.text: Accept the duel

ok.log: He is good. You are better, by one breath. He bows from the dust, sincerely, and leaves thinking very hard about his father.

fail.log: He wins, cleanly. Then he sits down on your step, confused, because you smiled when you lost, and asks why. You talk until dark.

choices.text: Offer him tea first, and the duel after

effects.log: By the second pot, he admits he does not even like his father's sect. By the third, he asks how you founded yours. The duel is postponed, indefinitely.

events.text: Three small sects of the county, each about your size, send their leaders up your hill together. Azure Pine has squeezed all of them. "A league," the eldest says. "Small sects, standing together."

choices.text: Join the league, as an equal

effects.log: Four sects, one oath, a shared meal at each new moon. The league is fragile, and the meals are excellent.

choices.text: Lead the league

ok.log: They agree, after some argument, that the youngest should lead because the youngest has the most years to do it. You accept the seat.

fail.log: They choose the eldest. You agree graciously. It turns out to be a relief.

choices.text: Decline. Your sect stands on its own feet

effects.log: They go home disappointed. Your sect stands on its own feet. Some winters, the feet are cold.

events.text: A league meeting at the new moon. The four leaders around one table, one jar, one problem: Azure Pine has bought the county's only pill-maker, and doubled the price for everyone not in blue.

choices.text: Pool the league's silver and hire a pill-maker of your own

effects.log: Forty taels from each sect, one cheerful old alchemist from the next province, and a furnace in your back courtyard. The league's pills are worse, and cheaper, and theirs.

choices.text: Send the league's disciples to gather herbs together

effects.log: Forty disciples of four sects, one hillside, three weeks. They come back sunburnt, with enough herbs and a hundred new friendships across sect lines.

events.text: An unsigned letter on the gate, nailed with a knife: Close your sect by winter, or we will close it for you. The knife is fine Azure Pine work. That is either very foolish of them, or very clever of somebody else.

choices.text: Investigate before accusing anyone

ok.log: The knife was bought in the market a week ago by a man from a third sect, hoping you and Azure Pine would bleed each other. You send the knife back to the buyer, wrapped in silk.

fail.log: The trail goes cold. Winter comes and goes. Nobody closes anything. You keep the knife on your desk, a letter-opener with a past.

choices.text: Post a reply on the same gate

effects.log: Under the knife you write: The roof leaks anyway. Come and fix it. The whole county finds this hilarious, which is a kind of armour.

events.text: A wandering master with a famous name stops at your gate and asks to see your best disciple. {npc} is pushed forward by the others. The master watches one form, frowns, and says to {npc}: "Wasted here. Come with me. I will make you a legend."

choices.text: Let {npc} choose, freely

mem.note: let me choose, and I chose home

ok.log: {npc} looks at the famous master, at you, at the leaking roof. "I will stay," {he} says. The master laughs, and leaves a manual on the step as a gift.

fail.log: {npc} cannot choose. {He} stays, but looks down the road for a month. Something has been planted, and it is not a demon seed.

choices.text: Step in front of {npc}: "My disciple is not for sale"

effects.log: The famous master raises an eyebrow, measures you, and bows. "A good answer," the master says, and leaves. {npc} trains until midnight.

events.text: Azure Pine's sect lord himself climbs your hill at last, alone, old, leaning on a staff that is also, plainly, a weapon. He looks over the yard, the new halls, the disciples. "When you came," he says, "I gave you three years. That was a long time ago."

choices.text: Offer him the master's seat for the afternoon

effects.log: He sits in your seat and watches your disciples train, and corrects one stance, and you let him. When he leaves, the feud is not over, but it has become something more like weather.

choices.text: Ask him plainly what he wants

effects.log: "Somebody to give the county to, when I am done," he says. "Not my son. He likes you better than me." You do not know what to say to that. He seems to find that satisfying.

events.text: Ding! Sect war declared. A rival sect's challenge letter lies on your table, sealed in red. Your disciples crowd the hall doorway, pretending to be busy, listening. Some of them have never seen a real fight. Some of them are very, very excited.

choices.text: Gather everyone and tell them the truth of it

effects.log: Nobody is required to fight, you say. Nobody here dies for a hill. Every single one of them stays. Afterwards you go behind the hall and sit for a while.

choices.text: Double the training and say little

effects.log: Dawn to dusk. Formations, footwork, the art of retreating together. Fear turns into sweat, and sweat into something like readiness.

choices.text: Seek out the rival lord, and try for terms

ok.log: Over a long evening, you learn why they challenged: a slight, years old, done by someone who held your hill before you. You cannot end the war, but you leave it smaller.

fail.log: The rival lord will not see you. You walk back up your hill in the dark, and start the training at once.

events.text: The night before the fight. {npc} cannot sleep and finds you on the wall, watching the valley. "What if I freeze?" {he} asks. "What if I run?"

choices.text: "Then you run toward me. Not away"

effects.log: {npc} laughs, shakily, and sits beside you on the wall. You watch the stars until the cold sends you both to bed.

choices.text: Teach {him} one breath to hold fear still

effects.log: In for four, hold for four, out for eight. {npc} does it until {his} hands stop shaking. Years later, {he} teaches it to {his} own disciples, with your name on it.

events.text: Scouts report the rival sect has sent a dozen fighters to hold the ford below your hill, cutting the road to the village and the rice. It is a provocation before the real fight.

choices.text: Clear the ford yourself

roll.foeName: the ford captain of the rival sect

ok.log: You walk down alone and ask them to leave. Their captain says no, then says nothing for a while, sitting in the river. The ford is clear by noon.

fail.log: You are driven back up the bank. The ford stays held for a week, and the sect eats thin soup.

choices.text: Find another way down for the rice

ok.log: A goat path, a rope, a night's climbing. The rice comes up the back of the hill and the rival fighters wait at the ford for a month for nothing.

fail.log: The goat path is a goat path. You get the rice up, with a twisted ankle and a new respect for goats.

choices.text: Send the village a message: stay home for a week

effects.log: Nobody from the village is caught in the middle. The sect tightens its belt. It is the right call, and an uncomfortable one.

events.text: Ding! Mountain-Guarding Formation raised. A low hum runs through the hill; flagstones shift themselves into a pattern you half recognise; the morning mist now rolls UP the slope against the wind and stays there, over the sect, like a lid.

choices.text: Walk the whole formation with your disciples

effects.log: Every flagstone, every turning. By sundown your disciples can find their way through the mist blindfolded, and any stranger cannot find it with both eyes.

choices.text: Test it: try to break in yourself

ok.log: It takes you all night to find the way through your own formation. You are proud and alarmed in equal parts.

fail.log: You walk in circles until dawn, and are found by the cook, who walks straight through to bring you breakfast. The formation, it seems, likes the cook.

events.text: The last war is over. The rival sect's banner, taken in the fight, is folded on your hall table, and a few of your disciples are bruised and smug. Their lord sends word: a formal bow, and a request to bury the matter. Your disciples want more than a bow.

choices.text: Accept the bow, nothing more

effects.log: A bow, returned. The banner goes back folded and unhurt. The murim notes that the upstart on the hill can win and stop, which is rarer than winning.

choices.text: Ask for their worst-treated disciple as the price

effects.log: A strange price. They send a skinny kid with a broom, who stares at your sect like it is a dream. You give the kid a bed and a real breakfast.

choices.text: Hang the banner in your hall

effects.log: It hangs there for years. Your disciples point at it for every visitor. The rival sect does not forget, and neither does the System, which files it as a goal met.

events.text: {npc} came back from the sect war with a wound, nothing a season will not heal, and something else, harder to see. {He} flinches at sudden steps. {He} trains alone, at odd hours. {He} has stopped laughing at the cook's jokes.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} in the evenings, saying nothing

mem.note: sat with me after the war

effects.log: Many evenings of silence and tea. One day {npc} starts to talk, and keeps talking, about all of it. The laughing comes back slowly, like a bird to a yard.

choices.text: Give {npc} a garden plot to look after

effects.log: Cabbages, then herbs, then flowers that serve no purpose at all. {npc} is out there at dawn, hands in the earth. By spring {he} laughs at the cook again.

events.text: Ding! A challenge is open, and the System makes a suggestion in red: Recommended: buy War Banner. Points: 60. The window then waits, looking innocent, like a shopkeeper beside an empty shelf.

choices.text: Ignore it. Prepare the way you always have

effects.log: You close the window and run the drills. The System reopens it twice more before dinner, the second time with a small drawing of a banner. You do not open the shop.

choices.text: Ask the System, sharply, whose side it is on

effects.log: Host's side, it answers. Always. And then, because it cannot help itself: The banner is very nice.

events.text: The rival sect lord comes to your gate after their defeat, alone and unarmed. "Two of my disciples are missing," the lord says. "Lost in your mist. I came to ask, not to demand."

choices.text: Go into the formation yourself and bring them out

effects.log: You find them by noon, sitting by a flagstone, cold and very sorry, sharing a rice ball. You walk them out by the hand. Their lord bows lower than you have seen anyone bow.

choices.text: Send your own disciples to find them

effects.log: Your disciples bring them out and share their lunch on the way. At the gate, four young people who were fighting yesterday are arguing about whose sect has the better cook.

events.text: Ding! Spirit-Gathering Array raised. Silver lines run under the yard overnight, a pattern like frost on a window, and the air over the hill grows thick and sweet. Your disciples wake up feeling as if they slept a week.

choices.text: Sit at the centre and test it

effects.log: Qi rises through the stones like warm water through sand. You meditate for one breath and lose a whole afternoon.

choices.text: Give the centre to the weakest disciple

effects.log: The weakest sits in the place of honour for a month. Something shifts, in the disciple and in the sect, which is not only qi.

events.text: Ding! Sect Banner raised. It arrives folded on your pillow, in the colours you once doodled in the margin of the sect register and never told anyone. The System is a great reader of margins.

choices.text: Fly it from the highest roof

effects.log: It snaps in the wind above the hill. Traders on the road stop to ask whose it is. In a year they will not need to ask.

choices.text: March it round the county at the festival

effects.log: Drums, the banner, every disciple in clean robes, and a very long walk in the sun. The county turns out. Azure Pine pretends not to notice, from upstairs windows.

events.text: Ding! Ancestor Pagoda raised. A small, perfect, seven-tiered pagoda stands behind the hall, and inside, on the first floor, one empty tablet with your name already carved on it. The System's sense of humour is sometimes dark.

choices.text: Burn incense there for your own masters

effects.log: You add tablets for everyone who taught you: the village sword teacher, the old herbalist, a beggar who once showed you a stance. The pagoda fills, and so do you.

choices.text: Turn your own tablet to face the wall

effects.log: Not yet, you tell it. The System says nothing, but the next morning there is a tiny carved smile on the back of the tablet.

events.text: The System has been showing the same goal for a long time. Every morning it greets you with it, every night it reminds you. Today it adds, under the progress bar, in small letters: Host may be interested to know that other sect lords complete this goal faster.

choices.text: Answer that you are building a sect, not racing one

effects.log: The window goes quiet for the rest of the day, which you take as an apology, and come to suspect was sulking.

choices.text: Ask it for a hint

effects.log: Hint, it writes: Do the goal. You stare at it. Then it adds, grudgingly, a real hint, which turns out to be useful.

choices.text: Work through the night on it, out of spite

effects.log: You train until the stars go out. The bar moves a hair. The System, you would swear, is smug.

events.text: A System error. The blue window flickers, shows a goal in a script you cannot read, a progress bar that runs backwards, and the words Sect name: Sect name: Sect name. Then it goes dark for a whole day. You are, for one day, simply a person who runs a sect.

choices.text: Enjoy the day

effects.log: You eat lunch slowly. You watch your disciples train without numbers floating over their heads. You notice things the windows never told you. When the System comes back, it seems to have missed you.

choices.text: Worry all day that it is not coming back

effects.log: You pace. You open drawers. You call it, softly, at the well. At dusk it comes back with a single ding, as if it had popped out for tea.

events.text: Ding! Bonus task issued: Make every disciple laugh in one day. Reward: unknown. You look at the window for a long time. Then you look at the sect: a row of exhausted, very serious young faces doing horse stance in the rain.

choices.text: Accept the task. Try everything

ok.log: It takes a song, a pratfall, an impression of a pompous sect envoy, and finally the cook falling in the well by accident. Every disciple laughs. The reward turns out to be the sound itself, and also a small qi pill.

fail.log: Eleven laugh. One does not, the most serious one, who watches your whole performance with folded arms. You do not complete the task. Years later, that one tells you it was the best day of training they ever had.

choices.text: Decline. Sect lords have dignity

effects.log: The task expires at midnight. At breakfast the next morning you trip over the cat, and everyone laughs anyway. The System awards nothing, pointedly.

events.text: Ding! Goal progress: a disciple of yours, {npc}, has reached Second-Rate. The System puts up fireworks only you can see. {npc}, who has no idea, is in the yard rubbing a bruised shin.

choices.text: Tell {npc} how far {he} has come

mem.note: told me I had come far

effects.log: "Second-Rate," you say. {npc} stares at {his} hands as if they belonged to someone else. Then {he} runs off to tell everyone, limping.

choices.text: Say nothing, and set the next mountain

mem.note: set the next mountain the same day

effects.log: No speeches. A harder form, a longer run. {npc} grumbles happily. Second-Rate is a step, not a seat.

events.text: Ding! Five missions completed. Sect Banner unlocked. Your disciples come back from the fifth, a merchant escort through the pass, sunburnt and proud, with the merchant's thank-you letter, which spells your sect's name wrong in three different ways.

choices.text: Frame the letter, spelling and all

effects.log: It hangs in the hall, the first gift from outside. Every new disciple is told to find all three mistakes.

choices.text: Write back, gently correcting the spelling

effects.log: The merchant writes back, apologising, and spells it wrong a fourth way. He also sends rice, which is spelled correctly.

events.text: Ding! Two halls built. The System offers you a tour of your own sect, from above, the way it sees it: dots of light that are disciples, a ring of qi that is the yard, a little blinking square that is the leaking north corner.

choices.text: Ask it to show you the sect in ten years

effects.log: It refuses. Future data restricted. But for one heartbeat before it refuses, you see more lights on that hill than you can count.

choices.text: Ask it to show you the sect as it was

effects.log: The hill as it was before you came: lights in every window of an old house, a child running in the yard. Then empty. Then one light. Yours. You close the window, very gently.

events.text: Ding! The System proposes an optional goal: Rename the sect to something more marketable. Suggestions follow: Heaven-Defying Supreme Sect, Ten-Thousand-Sword Eternal Sect, Very Strong Sect.

choices.text: Decline firmly

effects.log: Your sect keeps its name. The System, quietly, keeps the list, and brings it up again every new year.

choices.text: Adopt Very Strong Sect as an informal motto

effects.log: Your disciples love it. They shout it at the end of drills. Rival sects find it either deeply confident or deeply strange, and both are useful.

events.text: Your sect has grown past what one pair of hands can run. Two candidates for the first elder's seat wait in the hall: Elder Mok, a retired county inspector, strict and tireless; and Elder Ha, a former wandering doctor, warm, disorganised and beloved by everyone in the county.

choices.text: Appoint Elder Mok

effects.log: The accounts balance within a week. The disciples complain within an hour. Elder Mok bows to you exactly the correct depth.

choices.text: Appoint Elder Ha

effects.log: The infirmary is full of grateful villagers. The accounts are full of question marks. Elder Ha brings you tea every evening, which helps.

choices.text: Appoint both, and let them balance each other

effects.log: Two elders, one council table, and an argument on the first day about whether the table should face east. You have made a government.

events.text: Elder Mok and Elder Ha have not spoken in nine days. It began over whether disciples may eat in the training hall. It has become about the soul of the sect. Each sends a disciple to you every morning with a written position.

choices.text: Call them both to dinner, and lock the door

ok.log: Three hours, two jars, one locked door. At midnight they come out arguing about something else entirely, which is peace.

fail.log: They eat in total silence and leave by different doors. You eat both their desserts. The feud runs another month.

choices.text: Rule on it yourself: eating in the hall is fine

effects.log: Elder Ha wins. Elder Mok accepts, with dignity, and installs a crumb inspection. Somehow, both are satisfied.

choices.text: Ask the disciples to vote on it

effects.log: The disciples vote, and to everyone's astonishment, choose Elder Mok's rule: no food in the hall. "Ants," the senior disciple explains. Both elders are speechless, and reconcile out of shared shock.

events.text: Elder Mok has drawn up a reform: a sect hierarchy of nine ranks, with uniforms, a seniority list, and a punishment table. It is beautifully written, sixty pages long, and you can tell he has been working on it for years.

choices.text: Adopt it, in full

effects.log: The sect becomes orderly, efficient, and slightly less fun. Visitors are impressed. Elder Mok smiles, once, at the first full parade.

choices.text: Adopt the ranks, and burn the punishment table

effects.log: Elder Mok argues for the table for an hour, then quietly admits he never wanted to use it. The ranks stay, and are worn with pride.

choices.text: Thank him, and file it

effects.log: Elder Mok bows and says nothing. Two years later you find the sixty pages useful, and tell him so, and he says nothing again, differently.

events.text: Elder Ha has been treating the whole valley for free out of the sect's medicine stores, and the stores are empty. She looks at you over a pot of something steaming and unrepentant. "Sick is sick," she says.

choices.text: Back her. The sect pays

effects.log: Forty taels in herbs. The valley loves your sect fiercely from that year on. In the next sect war, three villages send their sons and daughters to carry stretchers.

choices.text: Set her a budget, kindly

effects.log: A monthly allowance, and a rule: the poor first. Elder Ha calls it bureaucracy and keeps to it almost exactly.

choices.text: Ask the valley to pay what it can

effects.log: Eggs, firewood, a goat, and some actual silver. Elder Ha is embarrassed by the goat. The goat stays.

events.text: An elder from a great sect, recently retired, asks for a seat on your council: a famous name, a powerful sword, and a reputation for taking over every sect that gives her one. She smiles at you as if you were already furniture.

choices.text: Give her a seat, and watch her

ok.log: She tries three times in a year to move the council. You outmanoeuvre her three times, politely. On the fourth, she laughs, and starts working for the sect instead of on it.

fail.log: Within a year half the council votes as she does. You win them back slowly, one dinner at a time. It is a long year.

choices.text: Decline, with every courtesy

effects.log: She takes the refusal gracefully and joins your rival's council instead. For years afterwards, you can feel her reading your moves.

choices.text: Offer her a teaching post, no seat

effects.log: She laughs at the offer, then accepts it, out of curiosity. She turns out to be a superb teacher, and to have no time left for politics.

events.text: The council meets on the first of every month. Today's agenda: a dispute over the well rota, a request for a new practice field, a complaint about the cook's soup, and Elder Mok's monthly motion to name the ghost officially.

choices.text: Go through it all, item by item

effects.log: Four hours. Well rota settled. Field postponed. Soup defended. The ghost motion fails again, three votes to two. It is the most boring and the most necessary afternoon of the month.

choices.text: Let the elders run it while you train

effects.log: You train. They govern. You come back to find the ghost has been named, and the soup has been reformed, and nobody will tell you how the votes went.

choices.text: Move the meeting to the hot spring

effects.log: Every elder agrees at once. The agenda is cleared in record time. Elder Mok is seen smiling, faintly, in the steam.

events.text: Elder Mok's quarterly accounts do not add up. Twelve taels are missing, every quarter, for two years. Elder Mok himself is the one who reports it, white-faced, with the ledgers under his arm and his resignation on top.

choices.text: Investigate before accepting anything

ok.log: The missing silver goes to the cook, who has been sending it to an orphanage in town every quarter and borrowing it from the ledger to do it. You tear up the resignation and add the orphanage to the budget.

fail.log: You never find it. You tear up the resignation anyway and cover the gap from your own purse. Some mysteries a sect lord simply pays for.

choices.text: Refuse the resignation outright

effects.log: "You found it. You reported it. That is the elder I want," you say. Elder Mok bows lower than the regulations allow.

events.text: The council wants to name a successor, just in case. The elders, each with a different disciple in mind. The argument has gone on all afternoon. Your own favourite, {npc}, is sitting outside the door, very visibly not listening.

choices.text: Name {npc}, and end the argument

effects.log: Silence. Then the eldest elder claps. {npc}, outside, drops a teapot. The council minutes record it as the decisive moment.

choices.text: Refuse to name anyone yet

effects.log: "Not while I can still lift a sword," you say. The elders grumble and agree. {npc} pretends not to be relieved, and is.

choices.text: Ask {npc} in, and ask if {he} even wants it

effects.log: {npc} comes in, red to the ears, and says {he} wants to be the best sword in the sect, not its lord. The elders write that down too.

events.text: A faction is forming. Half the outer disciples follow a charismatic senior who says the sect should leave the county league and stand alone, and that the sect lord has grown soft. The elders want you to act before it splits.

choices.text: Debate the senior in front of the whole sect

ok.log: You let the senior speak first, and fully. Then you answer. When the vote comes, the sect stays whole, and the senior asks to be your student again.

fail.log: The senior speaks better. Six disciples leave with the senior, down the hill, to found their own sect. You send them off with rice. It is how many sects begin.

choices.text: Give the senior a mission far away, and some responsibility

effects.log: A year guarding a merchant road in the north. The senior comes back older, quieter, and in favour of the league.

events.text: Elder Ha is old now, and has asked to step down to look after the herb garden. She hands you a box of notes: all her years of the valley's illnesses, cures, births and names. "The sect's real register," she says.

choices.text: Hold a feast in her honour

effects.log: Half the valley comes. Elder Ha is mortified and delighted in equal measure, and falls asleep in her chair before the last speech, smiling.

choices.text: Ask her to train her successor first

effects.log: A year more. She chooses a disciple nobody expected, and is right, as she was about most things.

events.text: In a morning spar, {npc} turns your sword aside with an ease that is no longer polite, and then stops, horrified, as if {he} had broken a precious bowl. You both know. {npc} has passed you.

choices.text: Laugh, and spar again, harder

ok.log: You lose again, but you make {npc} sweat for it. Afterwards you are both lying on the stones, laughing at the sky.

fail.log: You lose quickly. You learn more from that loss than from a year of wins, and tell {npc} so.

choices.text: Bow to {npc}, formally

mem.note: bowed to me when I passed them

effects.log: "Blue comes from indigo," you say, "and is bluer." {npc} cannot speak. That afternoon the whole sect knows, and is fiercely proud.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach you what {he} found

effects.log: Master and disciple swap places for an evening. {npc} is a terrible teacher, and you learn something anyway.

events.text: Visitors from another sect address {npc} as master and you as {npc}'s old teacher. Nobody means harm by it. It is simply true now. {npc} goes white and corrects them, loudly.

choices.text: Tell {npc}, privately, that you are proud

effects.log: {npc} does not believe you at first. You say it again. {He} does, the second time.

choices.text: Let it sting, honestly, and train

effects.log: It stings. You go up the mountain for a month. You come back stronger and lighter, and not jealous, which was the harder climb.

events.text: Ding! The System pops up during dinner: Disciple {npc} exceeds host. Recommendation: host should cultivate. The window then helpfully enlarges itself so everyone at the table could read it, if they could see it.

choices.text: Close it, and finish your soup with dignity

effects.log: You close it. It reopens, smaller. You close it again. {npc}, across the table, asks why you keep waving at the air.

choices.text: Take the hint. Seclusion, starting tomorrow

mem.note: went into seclusion to catch up

effects.log: A month in the cave behind the hall. {npc} brings food to the entrance every day and leaves it without a word. You come out a little closer.

events.text: {npc} has been offered an elder's seat at a great sect, with a hall of {his} own. {He} brings the letter to you unopened, and puts it on the table between you, and waits.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to go. A bird has to fly

effects.log: {npc} opens the letter. {He} goes. Every year after that, a letter comes back, and in the letters your sect's name is always spelled right.

choices.text: Offer {npc} the same seat, here

mem.note: offered me a seat at home

effects.log: {npc} laughs, the old laugh from the early years, and tears the letter in half. The council has a new elder, younger than any of them.

events.text: Your sect's goat has learned the first form. Not the whole form, just the opening stance and the charge. It now practises with the disciples every morning, and wins more bouts than the newest three.

choices.text: Register the goat as an outer disciple

effects.log: The goat's name goes in the sect register. Azure Pine hears of it and is furious for reasons nobody can quite articulate.

choices.text: Make the newest three train until they beat it

effects.log: It takes a season. The day the first one wins, the goat sulks for a week. The disciple frames the moment in memory forever.

events.text: The cook has a past. Today, a ladle thrown across the kitchen in a moment of temper went straight through a wooden door and pinned a fly to the far wall. The cook is pretending it didn't happen. So is the fly.

choices.text: Ask the cook, kindly, no questions about the past

effects.log: The cook looks at you a long time and says: "Soup's ready." A week later, unasked, the cook starts teaching the disciples knife work. Only vegetables. Officially.

choices.text: Ask the cook to teach throwing to the disciples

ok.log: "Ladles only," the cook says. Your sect becomes the only one in the murim with a hidden weapon art based on kitchen utensils.

fail.log: "I am a cook," the cook says, and serves you the worst soup of your life for a week.

events.text: {npc} can only fight well when hungry. Fed, {he} is sleepy and kind. Hungry, {he} beat three bandits last month with a fence post. Today is the county tournament, and the inn serves a famous breakfast.

choices.text: Keep {npc} away from breakfast

ok.log: {npc} wins every bout with a terrible expression and eats four bowls of noodles afterwards on the winners' step.

fail.log: {npc} finds the dumplings. {He} loses the first bout, and is very happy about it.

choices.text: Let {npc} eat. Wellbeing first

effects.log: {npc} eats, loses, and naps in the stands. On the walk home, {he} is the happiest person you have ever seen.

events.text: Every night, someone in the sect sleepwalks into the training yard and does a perfect sword form, then walks back to bed. Nobody knows who. The disciples are taking bets on it, which is forbidden, so they are taking chores on it.

choices.text: Stay up and find out

effects.log: It is Elder Mok. In his sleep he is a far better swordsman than awake. You decide never to tell him.

choices.text: Leave it a mystery

effects.log: The sleepwalker becomes a sect legend, the Night Sword. Visitors from other sects hear of it and are deeply unsettled.

events.text: A disciple has written a sect song. It has nineteen verses. It rhymes the sect's name with turnip. The disciples sing it on every march, and at the county gathering, and, last week, at a funeral, by accident.

choices.text: Make it the official anthem

effects.log: Rival sects mock it. Then they find themselves humming it. Then they are furious about humming it. It is unbeatable.

choices.text: Limit it to five verses

effects.log: The disciples negotiate you up to eleven, which is, they point out, a lucky number. The turnip verse stays.
