events.text: The training dummies have gone missing. All twelve. In their place, a ransom note in a disciple's handwriting: the dummies will return when the sect lord grants a day off. The note is signed The Dummy Liberation Society.

choices.text: Grant the day off

effects.log: A day of picnics and naps. The dummies reappear at dusk, freshly painted with smiling faces. They stay painted for years.

choices.text: Track down the dummies yourself

ok.log: You find them in the hayloft at midnight. In the morning the disciples find the dummies back in the yard, each holding a sign: Nice try.

fail.log: You search all night and find nothing. Morning: the dummies are back, wearing your spare robes. You grant the day off out of sheer respect.

events.text: A rival sect sends a famous swordsman to spy on your training. He comes back with a report: the goat leads warm-ups, the cook teaches throwing, the dummies are smiling, and somebody keeps singing about turnips. His sect lord does not believe a word, and comes to see.

choices.text: Give him the full tour

effects.log: The rival lord leaves pale and confused, convinced it is all an elaborate deception hiding a terrible secret art. You are not going to correct that.

choices.text: Put on a perfectly normal training day for him

ok.log: For one day, your sect is grim and orderly. The rival lord leaves, satisfied that his spy is mad. Your disciples celebrate with the turnip song.

fail.log: The goat ruins it in the first minute. The rival lord watches the entire chaos with his mouth open, and leaves without a word.

events.text: Two of your disciples have been feuding for a year over who is the sect lord's favourite. Today they ask you to settle it officially. One holds up a ranking chart they have made. The other holds up a counter-chart.

choices.text: Declare the goat your favourite

effects.log: Both disciples, united in outrage, spend the rest of the day plotting against the goat. The feud is over. The goat is unbothered.

choices.text: Say every disciple is your favourite on different days

effects.log: They immediately start a calendar. It is pinned in the hall. It is consulted, solemnly, every morning.

events.text: The manor ghost, it seems, is real after all. Every night someone sweeps the hall before dawn, folds the robes, and leaves the teapot warm. Nobody admits to it. The System, asked directly, displays: Data restricted.

choices.text: Leave a cup of tea out for the ghost every night

effects.log: Every morning the cup is empty and washed. Whatever lives in the Ma manor is now a member of the sect in good standing, with tea privileges.

choices.text: Stay up and watch

effects.log: At the hour of the ox, the broom moves on its own, very gently. You do not move. Neither does it, after a while. Then it goes on sweeping, around your feet.

events.text: Morning bell. Today the bell-ringer overslept, so {npc} rang it, enthusiastically, for a quarter of an hour, until the whole valley was awake, the goat was on the roof, and the village headman came up the hill in nightclothes.

choices.text: Make {npc} the official bell-ringer

effects.log: {npc} takes the job very seriously. The valley adjusts. The goat does not.

choices.text: Make {npc} apologise to the headman

effects.log: {npc} apologises at length. The headman, mollified, stays for breakfast and asks if a grandson of the house can join.

events.text: The disciples have entered the sect into the county's dragon-boat race. The sect owns no boat. Your disciples have built one. It is shaped, roughly, like a goat.

choices.text: Row in it yourself

ok.log: The goat-boat wins by a nose, its nose, and the crowd goes mad. The trophy stands in the hall on the hall shelf.

fail.log: The goat-boat sinks gracefully at the halfway mark. Your whole sect swims to the finish anyway, singing at the top of their lungs. They are the crowd's favourite by a mile.

choices.text: Cheer from the bank with the elders

effects.log: The goat-boat finishes fourth, which is better than anyone feared. Elder Mok is seen cheering, and denies it afterwards.

events.text: {npc} has been secretly practising a technique {he} invented, called the Thousand Turnip Palm. Today {he} shows you. It is, against all reason, quite good.

choices.text: Add it to the sect manual

mem.note: put my palm in the manual

effects.log: Chapter seven: the Thousand Turnip Palm. Visiting masters read it, laugh, try it, and stop laughing.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to rename it first

effects.log: {npc} renames it the Thousand Heavenly Turnip Palm. You accept this as progress.

events.text: Your disciples have decided you are an unfathomable master hiding your true strength. Every small thing you do is interpreted. You yawned at dawn; it was a lesson in breathing. You dropped a cup; it was a lesson in letting go. {npc} has started writing it all down.

choices.text: Keep up the act

effects.log: You say "Hm" at the right moments and look at distant mountains. {npc}'s notebook, The Master's Silent Teachings, reaches forty pages. Some of them are genuinely good.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the truth: you just dropped a cup

mem.note: told me the truth about the cup

effects.log: {npc} nods slowly, deeply moved. "Even the master's honesty is a lesson," {he} writes. There is no escape.

events.text: The disciples ask you to demonstrate the sect's ultimate technique at the festival. You have not invented one yet. The System window opens beside you, all innocence: Ultimate technique: not found. Recommendation: improvise.

choices.text: Improvise, magnificently

ok.log: Something comes out of you on that stage that you have never done before and could not do again for a year. The disciples weep. You go behind the hall and sit down very fast.

fail.log: You do a very long, very slow form, and then look meaningfully at the sky. The disciples debate its meaning for months.

choices.text: "The ultimate technique is not for festivals"

effects.log: The disciples nod solemnly. Your reputation for depth increases. You spend the next three years actually inventing one, in secret.

events.text: A wandering expert visits, takes one look at your sect, and announces to your disciples that their master is a fraud with a hollow core. Every disciple turns to you, waiting for the unfathomable master to answer.

choices.text: Answer with a single finger

ok.log: One finger, one touch, and the expert is sitting on the far side of the yard, blinking. The disciples will tell this story for years, and it gets longer every time.

fail.log: The finger is not enough. You need the whole hand, two sleeves and a lot of footwork, and you only just win. The disciples decide this was a lesson in humility.

choices.text: Ignore him with perfect serenity

effects.log: You go on drinking tea. The expert, unsettled by this, decides you must be hiding something enormous, and leaves in a hurry. Sometimes the act works by itself.

events.text: A retired officer of the county garrison, an old acquaintance from your travelling days, visits your sect and laughs until he cries. "You," he says. "Of all people. A sect lord. With a goat." Then he sees your disciples train, and stops laughing.

choices.text: Invite him to stay and teach

effects.log: He stays a season, and then another. He says it is the first place he has been since the garrison, where nobody wants anything from him.

choices.text: Share a jar and old stories on the wall

effects.log: You talk until the jar is empty about the old days, the bad postings, the friends gone. He leaves at dawn lighter, and so do you.

events.text: The System offers a deal: Mysterious Aura (temporary). Effect: disciples perceive the host as unfathomable for one year. Cost: nothing. The window waits. You suspect this is how the System entertains itself.

choices.text: Accept, out of curiosity

effects.log: For a year, every word you say is taken as profound. You test it by remarking that it might rain. The disciples meditate on it for a week. It does rain.

choices.text: Decline. You would rather be fathomed

effects.log: The System closes the offer, puzzled. That evening a disciple asks you an ordinary question and you give an ordinary answer, and it is the best conversation of your month.

events.text: {npc} has started copying everything you do: how you hold the cup, how you sigh at mountains, how you stroke a beard you do not have. The younger disciples are copying {npc}. The sect has become a mirror hall of your habits.

choices.text: Start doing something deliberately absurd, to test it

effects.log: You start hopping twice before entering a room. By the end of the week, the whole sect hops. You stop, out of shame. It takes them a month to stop.

choices.text: Tell {npc}, gently, to find {his} own way

mem.note: told me to find my own way

effects.log: {npc} is hurt for a day, then thoughtful for a month. Then {he} develops a style entirely {his} own, and it is better than yours.

events.text: Lecture day. Rows of young faces on the hall floor, waiting for the sect lord to say something wise about the Dao. You had prepared notes. You left them by the well.

choices.text: Speak from the heart

ok.log: You talk about the roof, and the drips, and how a sect is a thing everyone keeps from leaking. It is the best lecture you ever give. Nobody writes it down, so you never give it again.

fail.log: You ramble. The disciples are polite. One falls asleep, and you decide that, too, is a kind of peace.

choices.text: Turn it into a question session

effects.log: They ask about qi, about love, and whether the sect lord is ever afraid. You answer what you can. The best questions you take home to think about.

events.text: Accounts night. The iron chest, the ledger, a lamp, and a sect lord who would rather be fighting a tiger. The numbers do not want to add up.

choices.text: Grind through them

effects.log: By midnight you find a mistake in your favour. By the second watch, one against you. By dawn, the books balance, and you have a headache and a new respect for accountants.

choices.text: Ask a disciple who is good with numbers

effects.log: A disciple you never suspected of arithmetic does them in an hour, then explains them to you three times, very patiently.

events.text: {npc} and another disciple have been bickering all week: a borrowed brush, a moved mat, an insult about someone's mother's cooking. Today it came to blows in the yard. Both stand before you with matching black eyes.

choices.text: Make them carry water together until they talk

effects.log: Forty buckets in silence. On the forty-first, someone laughs. By sunset {npc} and the other disciple are sworn friends, and the trough overflows.

choices.text: Let them spar it out properly, with rules

effects.log: A real bout, with a referee and bows. {npc} loses, shakes hands, and the feud is over. The brush is returned.

events.text: Snow on the hill, the first of the year. The yard is white and silent and nobody has walked on it yet. Behind you, the whole sect is pressed to the hall door, waiting to see if the sect lord will allow a snowball fight.

choices.text: Throw the first one

effects.log: It hits Elder Mok, if you have one, or the goat, if you do not. Chaos follows. Nobody trains that day and nobody regrets it.

choices.text: Order morning forms in the snow first

effects.log: Forms in the snow, footprints in perfect patterns. Afterwards, the snowball fight is allowed, and it is better for being earned.

events.text: A disciple's family comes up the hill: two farmers in their best clothes with a basket of eggs, to see how their child is getting on. The child, {npc}, is trying to look calm and is failing completely.

choices.text: Show them {npc}'s progress in the yard

mem.note: showed my parents how far I had come

effects.log: {npc} does a form, perfectly, for the first time. The father cries. The mother pretends not to and gives you all the eggs.

choices.text: Invite them to stay for dinner

effects.log: They stay for dinner and tell embarrassing stories about {npc} as a child. The whole sect hears them. {npc} is mortified and happy.

events.text: Your sect's founding day comes round again. The disciples have planned something. They will not say what. Elder Ha, or the cook, or the goat, has been sworn to secrecy, and everybody is being very bad at it.

choices.text: Pretend to know nothing

effects.log: A banner, a song with too many verses, a cake shaped like the hall roof. You are completely surprised, which is easy, because you had guessed it was a cake shaped like the signboard.

choices.text: Plan a surprise of your own for them

effects.log: Fifteen taels of new robes, one for each disciple. They give you a cake, you give them robes, and everyone cries a little into the cake.

events.text: A traveller asks at the foot of the hill whether this is the sect with the turnip song and the kind sect lord. The villagers say yes, both, and send the traveller up. It is a young person with a bundle, asking to join.

choices.text: Welcome them in

effects.log: Your sect's reputation has reached further than you knew, and in a stranger shape. The traveller joins, and sings the turnip song by the end of the week.

choices.text: Ask which of the two brought them

effects.log: "The kind sect lord," the traveller says, then, honestly: "Also the song." You take them in.

events.text: Ding! Sect anniversary report. The System lays out your year in a long window: disciples trained, halls standing, missions completed, taels in and out, and one final line: Host smiled, this year: often.

choices.text: Read it all slowly

effects.log: You read every line twice. At the end you close it and sit for a while on the hall steps, looking at what you built.

choices.text: Ask the System if it smiled too

effects.log: A pause. Then: Data restricted. Then, a moment later, a very small yellow circle appears in the corner of the window, and vanishes.

events.text: A practice sword snaps in a junior's hands and the broken half spins toward the junior's face. {npc} is there first, arm up. The steel rings off {his} forearm like a bell. {npc} looks at the bruise, shrugs, and goes back to drills.
events.arc: The Porter Who Fell Off the Cliff

choices.text: Make {npc} the juniors' guardian at practice

effects.log: {npc} takes it as seriously as a temple vow. No junior in your sect is hurt at practice for years.

choices.text: Scold {npc} for not dodging

mem.note: taught me that an iron body still dodges

effects.log: "An iron body is a gift, not a plan," you say. {npc} learns to dodge, grudgingly, and becomes twice as dangerous for it.

events.text: At the county gathering, the crowd chants {npc}'s name before {he} has even stepped onto the stage. Rival sects glare. A child in the front row holds up a painted banner with {npc}'s face on it, badly. {npc} looks back at you, panicked.

choices.text: Nod once. Go and be seen

mem.note: told me to go and be seen

effects.log: {npc} walks out, and the noise doubles. {He} wins the first bout, waves at the child with the banner, and the child faints with joy.

choices.text: Walk out beside {npc}

effects.log: The master beside the star. The crowd quiets, curious. {npc} breathes again, and fights the best bouts of {his} life with you watching from the edge.

events.text: An Azure Pine elder offers {npc} a purse of silver to report on your sect's training. {npc} brings the purse straight to you, unopened, and asks what to do with it.

choices.text: Send it back with a polite note

effects.log: "Your silver," the note says, "was lost on our hill and found by an honest disciple." Azure Pine never tries it with {npc} again.

choices.text: Let {npc} keep it, as a reward

effects.log: {npc} spends it on new tiles for the north corner of the roof. You find out only when it stops leaking.

events.text: {npc} has opened a stall at the foot of the hill, selling the sect's spare herbs, pickles and, for a small fee, the chance to watch the disciples train. The queue is longer than the rival sect's recruitment line.

choices.text: Allow it, with a cut for the treasury

effects.log: The stall pays for the sect's pills that year. {npc} insists on calling it the Outer Treasury Pavilion.

choices.text: Close the viewing, keep the pickles

effects.log: The disciples are relieved. The pickles sell anyway. {npc} sulks for a day and then raises the price of pickles.

events.text: A notorious bandit chief comes up the hill to extort the little sect. At the gate you sneeze, very hard, and the old pine beside the gate sheds every needle at once. The bandit chief stares at the bare tree, then at you, and backs down the hill, bowing.

choices.text: Say nothing. Let the legend grow

effects.log: By market day, the story is that the sect lord of the hill can strip a pine with a breath. You did not know the tree was dying anyway. You never tell anyone.

choices.text: Tell your disciples it was the tree, not you

effects.log: Your disciples do not believe you. "So humble," they whisper. The legend grows anyway, with humility added.

events.text: The sect has acquired a rooster, nobody knows from where. It crows at the third watch, at noon, and whenever the sect lord tries to meditate. The disciples have named it Elder Rooster and give it a cushion in the hall.

choices.text: Accept Elder Rooster

effects.log: Elder Rooster attends every assembly for years and never misses a vote, by crowing. Its votes are, on balance, sound.

choices.text: Train yourself to meditate through the crowing

effects.log: It takes a season. After that, nothing in the murim can break your concentration. You consider this the rooster's gift.

events.text: An Azure Pine disciple arrives at your gate at night, in a torn blue robe, asking to transfer. Unhappy with the beatings and the fees, the disciple says. It could be the truth. It could be the oldest trick in the murim.

choices.text: Take the disciple in, and trust

ok.log: It was the truth. The transfer becomes one of your most loyal students, and the story of the blue robe on your hall wall makes Azure Pine's recruits think twice.

fail.log: It was the trick. The transfer is gone in a month, with a copy of your breathing chart and some silver. The chart is the false one. You were wiser than you knew.

choices.text: Send the disciple to a neutral sect of the county

effects.log: A safe home with no secrets in reach. Everyone wins, and nobody is sure whether it was a trick. It does not matter.

choices.text: Write to Azure Pine about the beatings

effects.log: Your letter is ignored. A month later Azure Pine's sect lord quietly retires the elder in charge of discipline. The disciple goes home, and writes to thank you.

events.text: A sect war is coming, and the disciples have painted a new banner overnight to carry into it. It is enormous. It is mostly the goat. Your sect's name is somewhere in the corner.

choices.text: Carry it into the fight with pride

effects.log: The rival sect sees a giant painted goat coming over the hill and loses some of its nerve. Your disciples are cheering before the first sword is drawn.

choices.text: Ask for a smaller banner, with the name bigger

effects.log: A smaller banner appears by morning. The name is bigger. So is the goat, proportionally.

events.text: Ding! Talent Beacon: a disciple has arrived. The System's message is followed, a beat later, by a second one: Note: the arrival is asleep on the doorstep. Host is advised to bring a blanket.

choices.text: Bring the blanket yourself

effects.log: A small figure curled against the gate, bundle for a pillow. You tuck the blanket round them and sit on the step till morning. The first thing they see in your sect is its lord.

choices.text: Wake the senior disciples to carry the child in

effects.log: Three seniors carry the newcomer in like a parcel of glass. The sect's oldest tradition starts that night: everyone who arrives asleep is carried in.

events.text: Ding! Sect audit. The System tallies the sect's possessions in a long window: one iron chest, twelve swords, a great many bowls used for catching rain, and one clay jar, sentimental value: high.

choices.text: Laugh, and close the window

effects.log: You laugh until a disciple comes to see what is wrong. Nothing is wrong. It is a good list.

choices.text: Ask it to count what matters

effects.log: A pause. Then a second list, all names: every disciple, the cook, and the gatekeeper's dog. Count: complete.
